metadata.title: Aim Where It's Going.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro af_bella) - per-beat mp3 durations are MEASURED, never estimated
metadata.greeting_note: hello lexicon. SKILL.md limits the HAI persona to the SHORTEST forms only - Hi / Ola / Hej / Ciao. The lexicon CYCLES least-recently-used first: Ola (05), Hi (08), Hej (09), Ciao (10), Ola (11), Hi (12), Hej (13), Ciao (14), Ola (15). Least recently used is now Hi, last seen at Ep. 12.
metadata.series_note: Ep. 15 was built as the finale because ideas.md listed Astronomy 01-15. The backlog has since been extended to 28, so the series continues; Ep. 16 is the first of the new block and the Notes section fences it off from Ep. 09 (denoising) explicitly.
metadata.target_runtime: Under 3:00 BY DESIGN. 425 words against Ep. 15's measured 0.3731 s/word predicts 2:38.6, leaving ~21 s of margin. The words-only model is noise of order +-5-10% with NO consistent sign - Ep. 06 +10.4%, 07 -0.4%, 08 -5.0%, 09 +2.7%, 10 -8.2%, 11 +3.3%, 12 -0.1%, 13 -5.1%, 14 +5.4%, 15 +5.2%.
metadata.purpose: Ep. 16 of the AI in Astronomy & Space Science series, from weekly_stem_videos/ideas.md Astronomy topic 16 (Adaptive optics that predict the sky - ML forecasting atmospheric turbulence milliseconds ahead so a deformable mirror can cancel the twinkle before the light is recorded). The episode takes the SERVO LAG ITSELF, because under frozen flow a delay is not a clock problem but a DISTANCE - and a displacement has a future you can read off its past.
metadata.boundary: ideas.md Notes: 'Ep. 16 is about real-time instrument CONTROL (moving a mirror), not cleaning up images afterward.' That fences it off from Ep. 09, denoising-deep-space, which is post-facto reconstruction. This episode never shows an image being repaired; every correction happens before the photons reach the detector, and B02 says so out loud.
metadata.color_semantics: Claude fidelity palette. Terracotta #D97757 marks THE SUBJECT OF EACH BEAT - the thing being examined - and ink marks the FIXED REFERENCE it is measured against. B03: the wavefront the mirror is HOLDING against the one that is really there. B04: the full-phase lag error against the part inside the correctable band. B06: time-only prediction against the spatial and combined bars. B07: one layer against three. B08: the servo-lag slice against everything a predictor cannot touch. The mapping never flips, so B03 teaches it once. Accented text is #A44A32; #B9B4A0 is strokes and fills only - never text.
metadata.distinct_from_earlier_episodes: Eps. 01-06 had AI inspecting observations; 07 standing in for a calculation; 08 a division of labour; 09 an output that was never a measurement; 10 a training set produced by past decisions; 11 an objective that omitted the failure; 12 an evaluation inflated by the split; 13 a positive class that does not exist; 14 labels that were a model's output; 15 a target that is partly a property of the observer. Ep. 16 is the first where THE MODEL MUST ACT BEFORE ITS INPUT EXISTS: the answer is wanted for a moment that has not happened, and the only reason that is possible at all is that the thing being predicted is translating rather than changing.
metadata.note: ILLUSTRATE LAW: the Claude UI appears at B00, B11, B12, B13. Every other beat illustrates its concept as a reel-local Manim scene (scenes.py). Plates come from assets/gen_ao.py, which synthesises von Karman phase screens, blows them across an 8 m pupil under Taylor frozen flow, projects onto 60 Zernike modes, and fits ridge predictors with lambda chosen on a held-out validation split and scored once on held-out test atmospheres. EIGHT claims are ASSERTED and the script writes nothing if any fails. Seed 1616. The headline servo-lag numbers are integrated EXACTLY from the spectrum rather than measured on the pixel grid, because a 1 ms lag at 10 m/s is half a pixel at 2 cm sampling. PUBLISHED (Keck II, Subaru/SCExAO, Doelman's prediction bound) and COMPUTED-HERE are kept apart on screen and in the voice. No LaTeX/MathTex anywhere. metadata.channel_title is omitted for the GATE V edge-bleed reason logged in Ep. 03. scenes.py is ASPECT-AWARE.
metadata.reformat: center-cut, focus-aware; pantry/<bid>-916.* is the human replacement slot; -916 overrides honored

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Om Mali. This video is about AI that forecasts atmospheric turbulence milliseconds ahead, so a telescope's mirror can cancel the twinkle before the light is ever recorded.

show.event: the composer types the ask on the cream stage
the send button arms in terracotta
running indicator: blowing phase screens across an 8 m pupil
three result lines land in order

props.command: An adaptive-optics loop needs about two milliseconds to measure the air and bend a mirror, and the air keeps moving. How much does that delay actually cost, and how much of it can a model predict away?
props.runningText: blowing von Karman screens across an 8 m pupil at 1 kHz...
output: the delay is a DISTANCE: 1.7 ms at 10 m/s = 1.7 cm of slide
only 16% of that error sits in modes a mirror can shape
predicting it away: 11x in clean air, 4.8x once the sensor is noisy

beats.narration_text: Sixteen episodes on where AI's answers come from. This one is about an answer that is always late, and what late really costs.

show.event: OM MALI writes in, terracotta hairline underlines it
role line fades in: Humanitarians AI - presenter
a card draws beside it
row one lands and is STRUCK: fifteen episodes / where the answer came from
row two lands boxed: this one / the answer is due before the question lands
series line: Ep. 16

beats.narration_text: Here is the whole idea. Adaptive optics measures the air, then bends a mirror to undo it. That takes two milliseconds, and the air does not wait. Prediction doesn't make the loop faster. It makes the mirror aim ahead.

show.event: a card draws on the cream stage
line one types: MEASURE THE AIR, BEND THE MIRROR, sub: two milliseconds, round trip
line two: THE AIR DOES NOT WAIT, sub: the correction lands on air that moved
line three lands in the accent and is UNDERLINED: SO AIM AHEAD, NOT AT
closer: before the light is recorded, not after

beats.narration_text: Start with what late means. Keck measures its own delay at one point seven milliseconds. At ten metres per second, the air slides one point seven centimetres. The mirror is holding the wrong copy.

show.event: the plate fades up: one wavefront cut in ink
PUBLISHED chip: Keck II PyWFS, 1 kHz, 1.7 ms measured
the terracotta copy is named: what the mirror is still holding
the two scale rules read out: r0 = 15 cm, slide = 1.7 cm
closer lands: same wavefront, wrong place

beats.narration_text: Frozen flow says turbulence travels rather than changes. So the lag error is the structure function, walked that far. The exponent comes out five thirds exactly. But only sixteen percent of it lies in modes a mirror can shape.

show.event: the plate fades up, terracotta curve first
the crosshair is named: coherence time 4.71 ms, one radian squared
COMPUTED chip: fitted exponent 1.666667
the ink curve is named: inside the correctable band
the terracotta connector counts out 16%

beats.narration_text: So predict. Take twenty-four frames of telemetry, fit one linear filter, and ask it for the frame that hasn't arrived. No physics inside, only the fact that a sliding pattern repeats itself.

show.event: twenty-four tick marks draw left to right: the history
a weight bar fans over them, tallest at the newest frame
an arrow jumps the gap to a terracotta slot: the frame that has not happened
the gap is labelled: 2 ms, the loop delay
closer lands: it learned the wind, not the physics

beats.narration_text: Where does the gain come from? Looking across the pupil in one frame buys twenty percent. Looking back in time buys fivefold. One snapshot cannot tell you which way the wind blows.

show.event: the plate fades up, six bars
the short soft bars are named: ACROSS the pupil, one frame
the terracotta bars are named: BACK in time, 24 frames
the ink bars are named: both
closer lands: a still frame has no direction

beats.narration_text: Then add sensor noise, and it collapses. Three hundredfold becomes eleven. With three layers of wind, under five. The atmosphere is not what limits prediction. Seeing it is.

show.event: the plate fades up, both curves falling left to right
the terracotta curve is named: one layer
the ink curve is named: three layers
the dashed rule is named: a realistic sensor
closer lands: the limit is the sensor, not the sky

beats.narration_text: Which explains the on-sky numbers. Keck reports twenty percent better residuals. That sounds small beside elevenfold, until you notice lag is only a fifth of the error budget.

show.event: the plate fades up, two stacked budgets
the terracotta slice is named: servo lag, about a fifth
the soft block is named: everything prediction cannot touch
PUBLISHED chip: Keck, 20% better SH-WFS residuals
closer lands: crush a fifth, move a fifth

beats.narration_text: The record agrees and complicates. With a vortex coronagraph, prediction doubled Keck's contrast close in. Four years later, on a different camera, Strehl came back merely comparable.

show.event: two dated rows draw, both PUBLISHED
row one fills terracotta: 2021, vortex coronagraph, contrast x2.03 at 3 lambda/D
row two fills ink: 2026, Brackett gamma, Strehl and contrast comparable
a hairline joins them and the shared fact lands: same predictor
closer: what you measure decides what it bought

beats.narration_text: The tell. I expected a messier sky to break it. Three layers in clean air still gave a hundred and eighty fold. Complexity was never the enemy. The filter fails only when the measurement does.

show.event: the expectation types in and is STRUCK: more layers should break it
two counters run up side by side: 1 layer 331x, 3 layers 183x
a rule drops under them: clean air
the same pair runs again under a noisy sensor: 11.2x and 4.8x
the verdict lands accented: noise, not complexity

beats.narration_text: So: the sky is predictable because it slides, and only as predictable as your sensor is quiet. The ceiling on aiming ahead is not the atmosphere. It is the light you have to aim with.

show.event: the artifact page draws on the cream stage
heading lands: A forecast, not a faster loop
five lines reveal in order

props.artifactTitle: Aim Where It's Going - one page
props.artifactHeading: A forecast, not a faster loop
artifactLines: Under frozen flow a loop delay is a DISTANCE: 1.7 ms at 10 m/s is 1.7 cm of sideways slide, about a ninth of r0.
The servo-lag error is just the structure function walked that far - fitted exponent 5/3 exactly, and 1 rad^2 at the coherence time.
Only 16% of it lies inside the 60 modes a deformable mirror can shape; the rest is fitting error no controller can reach.
A 24-tap linear filter removes 331x of the reachable error in clean air, 11.2x at a realistic sensor noise, 4.8x with three wind layers.
Looking BACK in time is worth 5x; looking ACROSS the pupil in one frame is worth 1.2x. A still frame has no direction.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Read it. Here is a control loop with a fixed delay; tell me which parts of my error budget prediction can touch and which it can never reach. Watch whether it separates the two.

show.event: the composer types the suggested prompt
the send button arms
three grading lines land

props.command: Here is a control loop with a fixed delay and an error budget. Tell me which terms a predictor can actually reduce, which are untouchable no matter how good the model is, and what measurement would tell the two apart.
output: grade it: does it separate reachable error from fitting error
grade it: does it ask about the sensor before the model
grade it: does it name a measurement, not just a method
